Summary

A request that needs more memory than the system grants now raises Python MemoryError instead of aborting the interpreter. I checked this end to end. I built the extension with cargo build -p treams-py --features extension-module (not maturin) and loaded it from a scratch copy of the package. Against the old extension, both subprocess cases die with return code -6 (SIGABRT). Against the new build both exit 0, printing "MemoryError: cannot allocate 36864000000 bytes" for sphere_cluster and "cannot allocate 9216000000 bytes" for field_operator. lattice.cube(3, 10**5) raises "cannot allocate 192002880014400024 bytes". A quick smoke script (sphere_cluster with its pullback, solve, eig, field_operator) still works.

Branch / commit: [agent id], commit 140a83d4 on top of 53299f80 (condensed into ae22657). The worktree started at 5dadf1d1 (now 76ed0e8), an ancestor of 53299f80 (condensed into ae22657), so I fast-forwarded to 53299f80 (condensed into ae22657) before starting.

Core error

  • Error::OutOfMemory(String) sits after Singular, with the doc line you specified.
  • pub fn Error::out_of_memory(count, element_bytes) -> Self gives "cannot allocate {bytes} bytes", or "cannot allocate more than {usize::MAX} bytes" when the multiply overflows.
  • is_numerical() is unchanged and returns false for the new variant; a test checks this.

Helpers

  • crates/treams-core/src/numerics/memory.rs is a private module, re-exported as numerics::{zeros, filled, reserve}:
    • zeros(rows, cols) uses checked_mul, then filled, then DMatrix::from_vec.
    • filled(len, value) reserves, then resizes.
    • reserve(&mut Vec<T>, additional) uses try_reserve_exact.
  • linalg::scratch(req: StackReq) -> Result<MemBuffer> is private and uses MemBuffer::try_new. An overflowed StackReq (alignment 0) gives the "more than usize::MAX" message.
  • filled has one caller outside memory.rs: the LU permutation buffers in Lu::new. Without a caller, the re-export fails clippy as an unused import.

Converted allocation sites

  • fields.rs operator: the 3·samples × modes matrix, plus the per-block column-slice Vecs.
  • cluster/spheres.rs cluster_parts: the coupling matrix. "cluster is too large" stays InvalidInput.
  • cluster/interaction.rs:
    • LocalMatrix::to_dense now returns Result. I dropped the single-block clone shortcut; it now always fills zeros and copies.
    • LocalMatrix::apply now returns Result.
    • Callers updated: operator, InteractionFactor::solve, solve_interacting, IlluminateResidual::pullback.
  • linalg/mod.rs: the LU factorization workspace and the forward/adjoint solve workspaces use scratch(..)? inside the existing threads::dense closures, which now return Result<()>. The permutation buffers use filled. I did not touch lu_workers, lu_threads, decomposition_workers or threads::product.
  • sw/expansion.rs: blocks() reserves dest_groups × src_groups (saturating_mul, so an overflow fails the reservation), and assemble uses zeros. I did not touch lines ~338-339.
  • tmatrix/sphere.rs and tmatrix/cylinder.rs: the dense T-matrix.
  • lattice/geometry.rs cube: try_reserve_exact becomes numerics::reserve, so the error is OutOfMemory instead of InvalidInput. "cube output size overflows" stays InvalidInput.
  • Tier 2, all done:
    • cw/expansion.rs Couplings::matrix now returns Result; both callers updated.
    • rotation.rs sw_rotation and cw_rotation.
    • ebcm.rs qmat.
  • treams-py/src/convert.rs matrix() now returns PyResult: it reserves fallibly, fills in row order, then calls from_shape_vec. All 12 call sites are updated in cluster.rs (4), iterative.rs, lattice.rs, linalg.rs (2), rotation.rs, smatrix.rs and tmatrix.rs (2). finish_periodic and finish_rotation now return PyResult.
  • context.rs error() maps OutOfMemory to PyMemoryError and everything else to ValueError. This covers detached and the ufunc guard.

Signature changes (all crate-private)

  • Lu::solve_in_place, Lu::solve_adjoint_in_place and Lu::solve_with now return Result<()>. Callers updated: interaction.rs (3), linalg/mod.rs (solve_owned, adjoint_rhs, EigResidual::pullback), smatrix/solve.rs (2).
  • LocalMatrix::to_dense and LocalMatrix::apply now return Result<DMatrix>.
  • cw::Couplings::matrix now returns Result<DMatrix>.
  • In treams-py, convert::matrix, finish_periodic and finish_rotation now return PyResult.

Docs

  • treams-core/src/lib.rs: the Errors section, which now also says which allocations are fallible; the Error and is_numerical docs.
  • treams-py/src/lib.rs: the GIL and Errors bullets.
  • context.rs: module doc, error and detached.
  • docs/design/index.md line 77.
  • docs/guide/large-clusters.md "Memory and time": a short paragraph rather than one line. It gives the peak of about four NM×NM complex buffers (64·(NM)² bytes: coupling, LU factors, solution, NumPy copy) and the note that the Linux OOM killer cannot be turned into MemoryError.
  • CHANGELOG.md: one bullet at the end of "### Fixed" under [Unreleased].

    • field_operator: 100k points on an lmax-30 basis, so 9.2 GB.
    • Each runs in a subprocess with TREAMS_RS_NUM_THREADS=2. The soft RLIMIT_AS of 8 GiB (capped by the hard limit) is set after the imports. The test asserts return code 0 and stdout starting with "MemoryError: cannot allocate ".
